name: Cosmelan peel
lead: Cosmelan is a professional depigmenting treatment developed by the Spanish company mesoestetic, marketed for melasma, post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation, solar lentigines and freckles.[1] According to Grokipedia, an AI-generated reference drawing on company material, it has two phases: an in-clinic mask left on for several hours, followed by roughly six months of home cream and sun protection.[1]

The company states it corrects existing spots and regulates melanin production, and is suitable for all phototypes; these are manufacturer claims.[1] No peer-reviewed trials of Cosmelan were found in the sources reviewed.

sections.h: Protocol as described by the manufacturer
paras: The professional applies the Cosmelan 1 mask, left on for a period set by severity, and the patient later begins a Cosmelan 2 cream regimen supported by barrier-repair products and high-SPF sunscreen. The company says the protocol was revised around 2024 to shorten mask exposure and delay the home phase.[1]

The manufacturer's consent form lists pregnancy and breastfeeding, product hypersensitivity, current oral isotretinoin, active infection, a history of hypopigmentation such as vitiligo, and open wounds as contraindications, with caution for a history of herpes simplex or keloids.[1]
No studies found. The company cites more than one million treatments worldwide, which is a usage figure rather than a study.[1]

card.summary: A mesoestetic depigmenting mask-and-cream protocol for melasma and spots; claims come from the manufacturer and no published trials were found.
card.note: Rebound pigmentation and irritation are discussed by the company, who stress sun protection; no independent studies found.

quick.overview:
Cosmelan is a professional depigmentation treatment from mesoestetic: a mask applied in clinic, then months of home cream and sunscreen. It is aimed at melasma and other pigment.

No published trials were found; information comes from the maker.
quick.mechanism: The company says it removes existing melanin deposits and regulates melanocyte activity.
quick.risks: Contraindications listed by the maker include pregnancy, isotretinoin use and vitiligo history; the company stresses sunscreen to avoid rebound pigmentation.
